items.text: Fereshteh Pezeshk said field evidence shows that the US, Israel, and the Islamic Republic are preparing for a new war, but all three sides are concerned about its consequences. Tehran has the ability to disrupt the energy market and regional infrastructure and uses this to deter the other side from starting a war. Washington's goal is to change the nuclear, missile, and regional policies of the Islamic Republic without collapsing the government structure.

Morad Vaisi stated that Israel's new national security doctrine is based on preemptive attacks instead of threat containment. Benjamin Netanyahu has planned a $145 billion increase in the military budget over the next ten years. Vaisi said that the overthrow of the Islamic Republic has become a goal in Israel's security policy.

Benjamin Netanyahu announced that Israel and the United States have united to confront the destructive force of the Islamic Republic. He said Donald Trump knows the ultimate goal of the ayatollahs is the United States. Netanyahu described his personal cooperation with Trump as historic.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, met with Sergey Lavrov, Russian foreign minister, in Tehran. They discussed bilateral relations and regional and international developments. They also explored ways to strengthen cooperation between Tehran and Moscow.

Niusha Saremi announced in the audio version of Titrawol that Putin's envoy is in Tehran simultaneously with Trump's threats. Tehran officials have warned about the possibility of war. This issue was raised in the Titrawol program.

Iran's Foreign Ministry summoned the German ambassador over accusations related to a plot against leaders of the Jewish community in Germany. Iran's deputy foreign minister called the accusations baseless and protested Berlin's stance. Iran stated these accusations will not deter it from pursuing Germany's international responsibility.

Fahemeh Najjar Ajam, a 29-year-old protester with a bachelor's degree in accounting, was killed on January 8, 2026, in Azadshahr, Golestan province. A video shows her mother's distress at her gravesite.

Mohsen Rezaei emphasized the importance of multilateral cooperation for maintaining regional security and stability in his meeting with Sergey Lavrov. He supported expanding strategic cooperation between Tehran and Moscow on regional affairs. Joint economic projects were also highlighted as contributing to regional stability.

Iran's oil terminals have been empty for over two months with no oil loading. According to Bloomberg, oil loading at Khark Island dropped from about one million barrels per day in July to nearly zero by the end of August. Since the naval blockade began, no Iranian oil tankers have passed through the Strait of Hormuz.

About 18 to 20 workers of the Neyriz overpass project have been laid off. The contractor cited unpaid company claims as the reason for the workforce reduction. Additionally, the representative of the Tabriz power plant retirees expressed concerns about the suspension of the association's accounts and the potential cut of supplementary insurance.

Iran's Foreign Ministry summoned the Irish ambassador as the representative of the EU presidency. This was in protest against the EU summit statement regarding Iran. Iran rejected the accusations in the statement and accused the EU of double standards.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad criticized the government's spokesperson's stance on the French police's treatment of protesters. He stated that Iranian authorities suppress protesters and issue harsh sentences. Mahdavi-Azad condemned the death sentences against Iranian protesters.

The death sentence of a convict in Karun was converted to blood money payment through an agreement between two families. The head of the judiciary in Alborz province announced reconciliation in 12 death penalty cases during the first half of the current year. These measures were taken to reduce the execution of death sentences.

The US Embassy in Yemen announced that in a meeting with Rashad al-Alimi, discussions were held about lifting the siege of Taiz, progress in the Yemen Dawn operation, and combating arms smuggling to the Houthis. The siege of Taiz has affected over one million civilians. Strengthening international cooperation to prevent arms smuggling to the Houthis was also discussed.

The disciplinary council of the Portuguese Football Federation has suspended Cristiano Ronaldo for 30 days and fined him 255 euros for leaving the national team camp in Denmark. Ronaldo can participate in the matches on November 14 and 17. The final decision about calling him for the upcoming games rests with the national team coach.

A citizen in a video to Iran International said that the Islamic Republic executes young people and buries their bodies in the deserts. He condemned this action. The video was released as a protest against the executions.

Omid Alishah, after the match with Esteghlal, said he is pursuing the complaint against Khodadad Azizi for insults through the same channel. He added that the Martyrs Foundation could also get involved. Alishah hopes the judiciary will take decisive action.

Netanyahu promised to end the work of the Islamic Republic in a message thanking Trump. The Chief of Staff of the Israeli army called a new round of war inevitable. Israeli media reported three possible dates for the start of the war in the near future.

Ghasem Rezaei, the deputy commander of the national police, stated that the country's policing strategy is asymmetric warfare. He emphasized maintaining internal security, combating organized crime, and being prepared for threats. He also highlighted the importance of engaging in soft warfare and protecting the people's beliefs.
In Mehr 1405, eight family murder cases were reported in various cities of Iran. A total of 31 people lost their lives in these incidents. Some of the victims were children.

Mikhail Mishustin and Mohammad Reza Aref discussed bilateral cooperation in the energy sector in Dushanbe. The main topic was the construction of the Bushehr nuclear power plant. This meeting took place during Mishustin's trip to Tajikistan before the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit.
Netanyahu stated that they are ready to strike at any moment. These remarks were made in the audio version of program 24 with Fardad Farahzad. No further details were provided in the text.
Donald Trump stated that Russia has taken no significant action to help Iran. He added that China and Russia's support for Iran has been minimal. Trump considered this a very positive turning point.

UEFA has given FIFA a deadline until November 2 to answer 42 questions about its management and decisions. The questions cover the private investment plan FFE, various cases, and negotiations related to FIFA cryptocurrency. Gianni Infantino apologized for the plan to delegate part of the World Cup's commercial activities.

French government officials have rejected the possibility of postponing the Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona match in the Champions League due to security conditions in Paris. The French Minister of the Interior stated that the match will take place as scheduled on Tuesday. This decision was made in response to security concerns and requests for postponement from some police officers.

Officials in Shabwah province reported that the death toll from the Houthi missile attack on a security forces training center has risen to 58. More than 200 people were injured and 14 remain missing. The Yemeni armed forces stated that the attack was carried out with three ballistic missiles.

Sergey Lavrov, the Russian foreign minister, arrived in Tehran on his first trip to Iran after the US and Israeli attacks. He met with Masoud Pezeshkian and Abbas Araghchi. Moscow has stated it is trying to prevent the escalation of the war.

Benny Gantz, former Prime Minister of Israel and leader of the Blue and White party, announced his withdrawal from the election race. Polls show a close competition between the coalitions supporting Netanyahu and Gadi Eizenkot. The role of Arab parties and the far-right movement has become significant in determining the next prime minister.

Mohammad Hassannejad, spokesperson for Tractor's board, threatened Malavan team regarding their number of spectators. Ashkan Pourrashid, owner of Malavan Bandar Anzali, responded that Malavan's fans are much more numerous than stated. They debated about the number and culture of their teams' spectators.

Jaber Rajabi said Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu have reached an understanding to end the threat of the Islamic Republic. Their goal is the overthrow or fundamental change in the nature and policies of the Islamic Republic. These efforts have broad support among political factions in Israel.

Asim Munir, the commander of the Pakistani army, is scheduled to visit Tehran on Tuesday. This trip follows his talks with Islamic Republic officials in the summer. Pakistan has played an important role in mediating between the US and the Islamic Republic this year.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, said that if a new attack occurs, Israel will carry out more surprising actions. Analysts close to the government have also confirmed this. Hamzeh Safavi stated that if the war starts, Israel might kill 1,000 to 1,500 officials.

The head of Iran's Chamber of Commerce warned that continued sanctions and economic restrictions could lead to business closures and widespread unemployment. Members of the Chamber cited factors such as power outages and internet disruptions as affecting business activities. They emphasized that without revising economic policies, improving conditions is difficult.

Morad Vaisi stated that supporters of the Islamic Republic held a gathering against the dollar where they intended to burn dollars. Hamidreza Maqsoudi also participated in this gathering. However, no real dollars were burned; all the dollars were just printed copies.

The US and several Western and Arab countries warned Lebanon to avoid involvement in a potential conflict between Israel and the Islamic Republic. Washington stated that if Hezbollah enters the conflict, Israel will respond strongly. The Lebanese president is continuing diplomatic efforts to prevent the country from being drawn into regional conflicts.

The Gulf Cooperation Council member countries held an extraordinary meeting in Saudi Arabia to explore ways to expand military cooperation and strengthen joint defense coordination. Participants emphasized increasing operational coordination and exchanging military experiences. The meeting aimed to enhance field cooperation among the armed forces.

Pete Hegseth, the US Secretary of Defense, visited Israel on Monday and met with Benjamin Netanyahu. The meeting took place eight days before the Israeli elections and amid talks between Washington and Israel about a possible resumption of military operations against Iran. The Pentagon and Israeli embassy declined to comment on the meeting.

Homayoun Shabankareh, a 22-year-old detainee in Karaj Central Prison, has been sentenced to death on charges of waging war against God and espionage. His death sentence was announced on October 17. He denies the espionage charges, and his case was handled by the second branch of the Revolutionary Court in Karaj.

The owner of Malavan Bandar Anzali explained that the cancellation of the match with Tractor was due to the injury of Shoja Khalilzadeh, which provoked the fans. He emphasized that the issue was personal, not ethnic, and accepted responsibility for the incidents. He also apologized to the people of Tabriz and called for the enforcement of the law.

The Washington Post reported that the Donald Trump administration has not approved the transfer of Patriot interceptor missiles to Ukraine, which are needed to counter Russian missile and drone attacks. The delay comes amid rising tensions between Trump and Volodymyr Zelensky. According to the newspaper, US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has not formally rejected the transfer but has also not completed the necessary steps to approve it.
Two large explosion waves occurred in Bandar Abbas at 4:10 and 4:12. Additionally, strange sounds and strong tremors were reported in the area. These events have caused concern among residents.

Japan has started a mission to explore Mars' moons with the MMX spacecraft. The spacecraft will reach Mars in August 2027 and collect samples from the moon Phobos. The sample capsule will land in Australia in 2031.

Donald Trump claimed in his speech in Kansas that the Islamic Republic has killed at least 75,000 protesters in the past eight months. He also said the Islamic Republic killed a world wrestling champion and hangs people with cranes. Trump emphasized that the US is conducting military operations against the Islamic Republic and will prevent it from acquiring nuclear weapons.

Donald Trump stated that the naval and air forces of the Islamic Republic have been destroyed, along with their radars and air defenses. He said the leaders of the Islamic Republic have been killed and the remaining officials have requested a halt to attacks. Trump also blamed the Islamic Republic for the deaths of Americans in roadside bomb attacks.

Axios reported that US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced visit to Israel on Monday, 27 Mehr, and met with Prime Minister Netanyahu. The visit took place eight days before Israeli elections, amid US-Israel discussions on possibly resuming military operations against Iran. Israeli Channel 12 also confirmed the meeting and recalled a report from a week ago about Netanyahu discussing with Trump the resumption of war on Iran.

JD Vance, the US Vice President, said the war with the Islamic Republic has entered a different phase. He emphasized that Tehran, after losing its nuclear capability and weakening militarily, is trying to limit the global energy supply. Vance also stated that if the US surrenders, the war could end quickly, but such a decision is not acceptable to Americans.

Pete Hegseth, the US Secretary of Defense, shared a photo of his meeting with US Central Command forces. He also made an unannounced trip to Israel to meet with the Prime Minister. This trip took place eight days before the Israeli elections amid talks about a possible military operation against Iran.

Li Qiang, China's Prime Minister, emphasized Beijing's efforts to establish peace in the Middle East and expand relations with Tehran during a meeting with Masoud Pezeshkian's first deputy. At the same time, Foreign Affairs magazine reported on military and intelligence cooperation between China and the Islamic Republic. This meeting took place on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit.

Mehdi Sarami Far commented on the IRGC's claim about seven internet cables passing through the Strait of Hormuz, stating that most of the traffic on these cables is related to the southern Gulf countries. He said damage to these cables does not necessarily mean widespread disruption of the global internet. Some of this traffic can be rerouted through alternative land paths.

Shahram Khaledi said a possible meeting of the leaders of the US, Russia, and China could cover issues such as the Ukraine war, the South China Sea, and nuclear weapons. He also questioned the fate of Ukraine and the Islamic Republic in potential agreements.

Mohammad Nayebizadeh warned that declining fuel quality, gas shortages, and increased mazut burning in power plants could worsen air pollution in Iran. The aging transportation fleet and increased suspended particles raise the risk of heart diseases, strokes, and lung cancer. This situation may turn this winter into a serious health crisis for the people.

Farzin Nadimi says the US and Israel are trying to make their alliance more public ahead of upcoming elections. The US defense secretary's visit to Israel and the presence of American fighter jets and refueling aircraft at Israeli bases are operationally and symbolically significant. These actions may indicate readiness for future joint military coordination.

Mohammad Qaedi said Russia's support for the Islamic Republic remains mostly diplomatic, and Moscow avoids actions that could lead to direct confrontation with the US. The increased risk of war and recent Russian diplomatic trips to Tehran may indicate efforts to find a political solution. These efforts might include issues like Iran's enriched uranium and restrictions on ship passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

A referendum on the future of Alberta, Canada's oil-rich province, was held on Monday, October 19. Citizens chose between continuing to stay in Canada or starting the legal process for a binding referendum on the province's independence. This issue was discussed with Ardshir Zarehzadeh.

An Australian media outlet reported that war and disruptions in transit through the Strait of Hormuz have caused problems for Iran's methanol exports to China. This issue was reported by Alireza Mohibi, a journalist from Iran International.

Financial Times reported that the Iran war has led to increased oil and gas production and exports in the Americas. Canada and Brazil have set new oil production records this year, and oil production in the US is also rising. US crude oil and petroleum product exports to Europe, Asia, and Oceania have increased by 15 percent.

Benjamin Netanyahu, the Prime Minister of Israel, met with Pete Hegseth, the US Secretary of Defense, on the evening of October 19 at Ovda Airbase. Representatives from foreign countries, possibly from the United Arab Emirates, were also present. Israel Katz and Shmuel Ben-Azra attended the meeting as well.

The head of Iran University of Medical Sciences stated that there are specific dress code regulations in universities, hospitals, and administrative environments that must be followed. If these rules are not observed, a warning is given, and repeated violations will be pursued. The initial approach to violations is advisory dialogue.

Reza Goharzad stated that Lavrov's trip to Tehran aims to reassure the Islamic Republic and encourage it to negotiate. Moscow emphasizes continuing its relations with Tehran and tries to persuade the Islamic Republic to come to the negotiating table.
An image shows students in a Tehran school tearing out a photo of Mojtaba Khamenei from their book. The photos were thrown into the trash. This event was reported by Iran International.

Ruhollah Rahimpour considered the US Defense Secretary's meeting with Israeli officials as a possible sign of military coordination between the two countries against the Islamic Republic. He stated that setting objectives, dividing operational roles, and coordinating threat assessments could be the main points of this meeting.
A video shows military equipment being transported in the streets of Sanandaj on the evening of Monday, October 19. This video was received by Iran International.

Adel Ferdosipour responded to Amir Ghalenoei's criticisms about his program's financial income, stating that the money he receives from sponsors is less than Ghalenoei's bonus for leading the national team to the World Cup. He emphasized that this money is shared among 100 colleagues and that the financial transparency of his activities has been monitored by regulatory bodies. Ferdosipour also stated that financial matters are not important to him.

Mohammad Bayat stated that any military adventurism by the US will turn the Persian Gulf into a graveyard for invading ships. Iranian armed forces are fully prepared and any US military action will be met with a decisive response. He also emphasized that US military movements will not weaken the Iranian nation's resolve and will impose heavy costs on Washington.

Dalga Khatinoglu warned that the daily reduction of 100 to 130 million cubic meters in Iran's gas production after the war will make energy supply in winter more difficult. She said that increasing the use of mazut and diesel cannot compensate for this deficit. This will also lead to increased air pollution.
Nahid Khodajoo, a labor activist, has been detained in Karaj's Kachouyi prison for over two weeks. Her detention continues. This report was published by Harana News Agency.

Ismail Baqaei, the Foreign Ministry spokesperson, stated that the Islamic Republic will not leave any attack unanswered and that the era of hit-and-run is over. He also mentioned that Lavrov's visit to Tehran was planned and no discussions about nuclear negotiations with the US took place. Baqaei advised Gulf countries' officials to be more cautious in their statements.

Volodymyr Zelensky criticized the new US stance on military and intelligence support for Kyiv, stating that the Pentagon has delayed delivery of missiles already paid for by Ukraine's allies. He also proposed halting attacks on Russian oil refineries for 30 days in exchange for receiving Patriot interceptor missiles.

The Champions League match between Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona will be held as scheduled on Tuesday evening at the Parc des Princes. French officials have dismissed rumors of postponement or cancellation due to recent unrest. The French Interior Minister stressed that the issue of postponing the match is not on the table at all.

Gholamhossein Karbaschi, the editor of Ham Mihan newspaper, was found guilty for publishing certain content. Mehdi Rahmanian, the editor of Shargh newspaper, was acquitted of the charges. These rulings were issued by the political and press court jury.

Hossein Aghaei considered the US Defense Minister's trip to Israel and his meeting with Netanyahu as a sign of the importance of military coordination between the two countries. He outlined two scenarios for a possible attack on the Islamic Republic: limited airstrikes or a large-scale operation aimed at regime change. These statements were published by Iran International.

On the evening of Monday, October 27, the home of Milad Aqdasi and Samieh Qolinejad, a Baha'i couple living in Yazd, was searched by security forces. During the search, a number of their personal belongings were confiscated. An informed source said agents entered the home around 11 PM and continued the search until 3 AM.

A video has been released showing the parents of Mohsen Abbasi paying respects at the grave of Masoud Zatparvar. Mohsen Abbasi, 21 years old, was killed on January 7, 2026, in Najafabad. Masoud Zatparvar, 39 years old and a bodybuilding champion, was killed the same day in Rasht.

Ali Shirazi from Iran International stated that the Islamic Republic has formed a hijab task force in universities. The goal is to prevent protest movements through disciplinary restrictions and pressure on students. Also, mandatory hijab is no longer a tool for the government to display power.

Mohammad Hasanvand, head of the regulations drafting committee of the Football Federation, announced a decision to intensify disciplinary penalties and move towards punishments such as point deductions and suspensions. He said current financial fines are no longer deterrent and called for heavier sanctions for offending managers. The disciplinary committee has also invited managers of both Malavan and Tractor clubs to a meeting on Thursday to provide explanations about the match incidents.

Reports indicate that foreign insulin and regular insulin have become scarce in reference pharmacies. Citizens have sent videos showing the shortage of this medicine and rationing of access to it. This issue has been reported by Iran International.

Seven days before the Israeli elections, the competition between Benjamin Netanyahu, Gadi Eisenkot, and Naftali Bennett is very close. Eisenkot, with the Yesh Atid party, has become a serious rival to Netanyahu and holds a tough stance against the Islamic Republic. Polls show that no bloc has the necessary majority, and the outcome depends on the support of other parties.

Karim Jafari, a protester arrested in January 2026 and sentenced to 16 years in prison, sent an audio message to his eight-year-old son expressing his wish for him to be strong. He also told the people of Iran that now is the time to act. Jafari expressed hope that Iran will be free soon.

The French Prime Minister stated that curfews in several cities have helped reduce nighttime unrest, and the government will decide on expanding these restrictions. In Italy, the Deputy Prime Minister announced that 500 army forces will be deployed to secure Milan. These measures follow ongoing violent protests in both countries.

Reuters, citing Iranian sources, reported that Tehran believes Trump is ready to resume military attacks. Iran is preparing for continued attacks by Israel and the US and does not intend to reach a peace agreement. The chance of progress in negotiations before the elections is low.

Ali Abdollahi warned that if a new war against Iran begins, its fire will affect everyone. He warned Donald Trump and Israel against actions against the Islamic Republic and stated that the armed forces will target American interests. He also advised the International Atomic Energy Agency to refrain from baseless statements about Iran's nuclear sites.

Long fuel queues continue in many areas of Iran. An official stated that identity verification and a fuel fee are required to receive free-market gasoline. Ata Hosseinian described these measures as demand suppression.

Hassan Qashqavi stated that nuclear issues are not currently on the diplomatic agenda. The Islamic Republic's position on the Strait of Hormuz involves accepting conditions announced by the US. The Pakistani army commander's visit to Tehran is unrelated to mediation efforts regarding the Strait of Hormuz.
Today, Tuesday, 28 Mehr, a landmine explosion from the Iran-Iraq war occurred in Sarpol-e Zahab. Three citizens were injured in this incident. The explosion was caused by leftover mines from the war.

Salman Es'haqi, spokesperson for the Health and Treatment Commission of the Parliament, stated that the US will definitely carry out attacks on Kuh-e Kalang. He mentioned the possibility of renewed conflicts based on the historical record of the US and Israel. He also noted that a response with an 18-year annex has been designed for a possible attack on nuclear infrastructure.

Despite ongoing tensions and unrest in Paris, the French Interior Minister rejected the possibility of postponing or canceling the crucial Tuesday night match between Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona, announcing that the match will be held as scheduled.

A citizen sent a video showing the presence of agents and a severe security atmosphere in Borujerd. He says the forces have come to prevent the regime's fall. The citizen believes the regime's fall is inevitable.

Bloomberg reported that the Royal Air Force of Britain is deploying its fighters to Saudi Arabia. This is part of defensive missions to counter Houthi attacks. More details were provided in an interview with Tajeddin Soroush.

Cristiano Ronaldo was suspended for thirty days and fined 255 euros for unexpectedly leaving the Portugal national team camp. This decision by the Portuguese Football Federation has sparked criticism from the media and concerns about internal contradictions. Newspapers highlighted the inconsistent treatment of players and lack of transparency in decisions.

On the morning of Monday, 27 Mehr, heavy pollution and dust put the sky of Khuzestan in a critical condition. The air quality index in Ahvaz reached 160, placing it in the red and unhealthy category for all age groups. The Khuzestan Environmental Protection Department warned that 11 other cities in the province have similar conditions and residents should avoid unnecessary travel.

Hossein Mohebbi, spokesman for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, identified the communication cables under the Strait of Hormuz as 'new targets' for IRGC attacks and threatened that any new U.S. military action would cause a 'serious energy crisis' for the world.

Muslim Yaghoubi, the legal deputy of the army, stated that the pilots are alive and the Qatari government has not provided any document about their death. The army considers the International Committee of the Red Cross responsible for following up on the pilots' status. This issue is being pursued through international authorities.

The human rights media outlet Hal-Wash reported the deployment of military forces, armored vehicles, and a military helicopter in the border county of Golshan. The helicopter has landed in the area. The reason and duration of the deployment are still unknown.

The time and venue of the first derby between Esteghlal and Persepolis in the women's Premier League have been changed. The match was postponed from Friday, October 23 to Wednesday, October 27 at Shahr Qods Stadium. The delay was due to the Security Council's objection and the need for a better-equipped stadium.

Reuters, citing three senior Iranian officials, reported that the Islamic Republic deliberately prolonged negotiations with the US. The aim was to increase political pressure on Donald Trump and influence the US midterm congressional elections. More details were provided in an interview with Maryam Rahmati.

A citizen sent a voice message to Iran International about increasing inflation and severe economic pressure in Iran. He said that people's patience is running out. This indicates public dissatisfaction with the economic situation.

Benny Gantz, former Israeli defense minister and leader of the Blue and White party, withdrew from the parliamentary elections one week before the vote. This news was announced ahead of the important Israeli elections. Behrouz Yousian, a Middle East researcher, has evaluated the issue.

The One Million Signatures campaign in the 1380s aimed to bring women's legal equality to everyday life. However, security and judicial repression limited the campaign's activities and changed its course. These repressions affected the organization and trust among activists.

The UK Ministry of Defence announced that Typhoon fighters will carry out defensive missions to protect cities and critical infrastructure in Saudi Arabia against air attacks by the Houthis. These fighters will only have defensive missions and will not conduct offensive attacks. Additionally, a transport aircraft and military advisors will be sent to Saudi Arabia.

At the end of the second day of the 2026 Nagoya Para Asian Games, Iranian athletes won 30 medals. These medals include 7 gold, 9 silver, and 14 bronze. Iran rose to fifth place in the medal distribution table.

Emmanuel Macron, the President of France, met with Sheikh Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa in the Sakheer region. This meeting is part of Macron's regional trip to Gulf countries, including Kuwait, the UAE, and Qatar. The discussions focused on the situation in the Strait of Hormuz and its impact on energy prices.

Jalil Badamfirouz stated that air pollution causes about 50,000 deaths annually in the country. He also mentioned that environmental crises such as water resources and land subsidence have reached a critical stage. These statistics are based on data from the Environmental Protection Organization and the Ministry of Health.
Moein Ahkami, a student at Khajeh Nasir al-Din Tusi University, was sentenced to two semesters of suspension from studies by the university's preliminary council.

The UK Ministry of Defence announced that the Royal Air Force is participating in defensive missions against Houthi attacks. A spokesperson for the Saudi-led military coalition reported intercepting and destroying a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis towards Riyadh. These details were shared in an interview with an Iran International reporter.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated that the government was supposed to spend 12 billion dollars on gasoline imports but has only spent two to three billion dollars, with the rest saved. He also mentioned a 10 billion dollar saving in the energy sector. The income from gasoline price increases is promised to be allocated to people's ration cards.

The head of Qazvin traffic police reported a 41% increase in fatal accidents and a 43% rise in deaths in urban roads. Forty percent of the deceased were pedestrians and 28% were motorcyclists. Most accidents occurred in Qazvin county, and the promise to build 13 pedestrian bridges was not fulfilled.

Volodymyr Zelensky, President of Ukraine, is meeting with Steve Whitcuff, the US special envoy, during his trip to Oslo. The aim of the talks is to reduce tensions and improve Kyiv-Washington relations. Officials from Norway and Finland are also attending the meetings to discuss the Russia-Ukraine war and European security.

A meeting is being held in Oslo, Norway, with representatives of the Trump administration and several European leaders. This meeting takes place amid ongoing diplomatic efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war. More details are provided in an interview with Mehran Abbassian.

Scott Bessent said the pressure to economically isolate Iran has reached an unprecedented level. He stated that since August, no oil shipments have been observed at Khark Island and Iran currently has no oil on water. Additionally, the rial's value has dropped and inflation has exceeded 100 percent.

French cybersecurity agencies have identified traces of the Islamic Republic in the activity of French-speaking X network accounts during recent protests. The Macron government has refrained from publicly releasing these findings. More details are provided in an interview with an Iran International reporter.

The police commander of Torghabeh-Shandiz announced the arrest of two individuals accused of setting a guard dog on fire during a villa theft. Further details and the condition of the injured dog have not been released.

Israel's Defense Minister Yisrael Katz stated that the Israeli army will not withdraw from the security zone in southern Lebanon until Hezbollah is disarmed and threats against northern Israel are eliminated. He warned that any attack on Israel will be met with a strong response, and the army is prepared to advance further in southern Lebanon. Occupied areas will be evacuated and permanently added to Israel's security zone.

A men's barbershop in Esfarayen was closed for providing services to female customers. The operator was arrested and a case was filed against him. The case has been referred to the judicial authority.

Satara has filed a complaint against the director, producer, manager, and broadcasting platform of the series "Badnam" to the Ethical Security Prosecutor's Office. The complaint concerns episode 25, where a character named "Yalda" appears with shaved hair. This action was taken two weeks after the series finished airing.

The spokesperson of Iran's Foreign Ministry considered Trump's response to Tehran's agreement proposal insufficient. The spokesperson of the Revolutionary Guards named seven submarine internet cables as main targets in the next war. Tehran also warned that it would fire missiles at the heart of Europe.

Javad Gharaei released a video of the search and rescue operation of two Yak-130 fighter pilots in Esfand 1404. The fighter was targeted during the recent war between the Islamic Republic and Israel and the US. The two pilots ejected and landed in the Alborz mountains near Lavasan.

A special poll has been held to select the best individual season of Ballon d'Or winners in football history. Cristiano Ronaldo leads the temporary results with 62% of votes for his 2008 performance. This poll is held to mark the 70th anniversary of the Ballon d'Or award.

The third week of the UEFA Champions League starts on Tuesday with 9 matches. The most important match is Paris Saint-Germain hosting Barcelona. This game will be held in Paris with strict security measures.

The deputy of political, security, and social affairs of Rudan announced the identification of 45 children who have dropped out of first grade. Serious illnesses and migration were cited as reasons for some students dropping out.

According to initial estimates, the vast majority of participants in Alberta's referendum opposed the province's separation from Canada. About 76% voted to remain in Canada, while 24% supported a final referendum on independence. The report was provided by Mahsa Mortazavi from Iran International.

The spokesperson for the US Central Command stated that the Strait of Hormuz is completely open and safe, with 95% of ships successfully passing through. He said the US and regional partners control the strait, while the Islamic Republic continues its attacks. Additionally, the US is enforcing a blockade on Iran and has weakened the capabilities of the IRGC.

Tasnim News Agency reported, citing a security source, that Ukraine has deployed drone forces in countries surrounding Iran, including the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. Tehran considers this move part of hostile actions by Europe and NATO against the Islamic Republic. Iran has considered an appropriate option to respond to this action.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated in a meeting with the Pakistani army commander that the US can only gain Tehran's trust by fulfilling Iran's seven conditions. He added that threats and military movements cannot change the strategic decisions of the Islamic Republic. Ghalibaf emphasized that the US must take action to get out of the quagmire of war.
Hadi Jamshidi, a philosophy student at the University of Tehran, was summoned to the Ministry of Intelligence's follow-up office.

Mohsen Rezaei stated that no enriched nuclear material will leave Iran and that these materials remain a national wealth for domestic use. He also said that negotiations with the US will only begin after Iran's conditions are met and trust is established. These remarks were made during a meeting with the Pakistani army commander.

Different reports have been published about Alireza Beiranvand's military service destination. His service location code has been assigned to the Revolutionary Guards, but the Army club has also negotiated to recruit him. Beiranvand's final destination for military service is still unknown.

British police have arrested a 24-year-old British citizen and a 25-year-old dual Iranian-British citizen on suspicion of cooperating with the Islamic Republic's intelligence service. These arrests were made as part of investigations into suspicious activities at the RAF Fairford base last month.
Five workers were injured in three work accidents in Nazarabad, Ardabil, and Rasht. Three miners suffered gas poisoning in a sewage well. Two construction workers were injured due to a fall.
